thesis_text: Bottom line: Figma is a strong target for builders who can show craft in real-time, collaborative product engineering — and for students it has the clearest official early-career on-ramp in this batch (mentored 12-16 week internships that convert). The constraint is focus: published application limits punish spray-and-pray. Who gets in (sourced numbers only): no hire-population numbers are claimed — school/feeder/major shares are omitted for lack of a public sample. Sourced numbers are official posting/page facts: internships of 12-16 weeks at 40 hours/week, a C++ SWE base range of $153,000-$376,000 (a multi-level band), and application limits of 5 per 30 days with a 90-day same-role reapply wait. Stated vs revealed screens: Figma states 'Grow as you go', language-agnostic DS&A for early career, and product mindset/UX attention for experienced roles. Engineer reports reveal the experienced loop's weight on Figma-flavored practical coding, two system-design rounds (run in Figma), and a slides-based project deep dive — and anecdotal advice that referrals help, which is unquantified. Ranked entry routes: (1) SWE intern via the early-career page for students, (2) early-career full-time engineering roles, (3) direct application to one specific experienced posting, (4) referral as an unquantified accelerant. Timeline/dates (as of 2026-10-12): Summer 2027 SWE intern roles were listed at fetch; intern cohorts start January (winter) and May/June (summer); engineer-reported experienced process is about 3-4 weeks. Re-verify next cycle. Risks/alternatives: the one-role-at-a-time focus that engineer reports describe, plus hard application caps, means a mistimed application costs a cycle; design-tool and real-time collaboration peers are the natural hedge. Gap analysis vs a specific user is not computed here (no population sample).
known_biases_of_data: Survivorship bias: the official early-career page showcases successful intern-to-full-time conversions only.
Self-report bias: experienced-loop detail comes from engineer conversations compiled by a third party, not Figma HR.
Official postings describe the band and requirements for specific roles; the wide C++ salary band must not be read as typical or entry-level pay.

No H-1B LCA, university-outcome or licensed population data was fetched in this pass; the early-career page notes immigration sponsorship may be available for eligible roles, which is not a sponsorship pattern.
